questions.q_figure: Five small pictures in a row: a flower, a butterfly, a rangoli, a pinwheel and a cloud, with no lines drawn on them.
questions.s_figure: The same five pictures with each line of symmetry drawn as a dashed line: six on the flower, four on the rangoli, one on the butterfly, none on the pinwheel and none on the cloud.

questions.q_figure: Five outline figures in a row: an arrow-head shaped pentagon with a notch, a kite, a four-sided figure with two right angles and a slanted top, an L-shape and a scalene triangle.
questions.s_figure: The same five figures with each line of symmetry drawn as a dashed line.

questions.name: Many Lines: folds and lines of a square
questions.s_figure: A square with its four lines of symmetry drawn as dashed lines: one vertical, one horizontal and the two diagonals.

questions.name: Many Lines: diagonal of a rectangle
questions.q_figure: A rectangle that is longer than it is wide, with one diagonal drawn as a dashed line.
questions.s_figure: The rectangle cut along the diagonal into two triangles, one laid over the other with the corners not meeting.

questions.q_figure: A square standing on one corner and an eight-pointed star side by side for part (a), an equilateral triangle for part (b) and a regular hexagon for part (c).
questions.s_figure: The same shapes with every line of symmetry drawn as a dashed line.

questions.q_figure: Eight outline figures: four rhombus patterns (one rhombus above two, three rhombi in a row, a large diamond of four rhombi, two columns of two overlapping rhombi) and four red shapes on squared grids (a square inside a larger square with the inner square split into four, an octagon with long vertical sides, a five-sided kite-like shape, a four-pointed star).
questions.s_figure: The same eight figures with each line of symmetry drawn as a dashed line.

questions.q_figure: A large six-sided kolam made of dots and star shapes built from rhombi, with the same design repeating around its centre.
questions.s_figure: The kolam with its lines of symmetry drawn as dashed lines through the centre.
Three triangles, each with its lines of symmetry drawn as dashed lines: one with exactly one line, one with exactly three lines and one with none.
Three figures with curved boundaries, each with its lines of symmetry drawn as dashed lines: one with exactly one line, one with exactly two and one with exactly four.

questions.name: Reflection: square ABCD in a diagonal
questions.q_figure: A square with corner A at the top left, B at the top right, C at the bottom right and D at the bottom left.
questions.s_figure: Two copies of the square: one with the diagonal AC dashed, A and C staying put and B and D swapped, and one with the horizontal middle line dashed and the top corners swapped with the bottom corners.

questions.q_figure: Six squared-paper grids (a) to (f), each with a blue line and a red part-outline on one side of it, and in (a) the outline is already completed as a dashed mirror image across a vertical blue line.
questions.s_figure: Each grid with the red outline completed on the other side of the blue line as its mirror image.

questions.q_figure: Six squared-paper grids (a) to (f), each with two blue lines (two diagonals in (a) and (b), a vertical and a horizontal line in (c) to (f)) and a red part-outline in one region.
questions.s_figure: Each grid with the red outline reflected in both blue lines so that the completed figure is symmetric about both.

questions.q_figure: Six dot grids, each with a few connected line segments drawn between the dots.
questions.s_figure: Each dot grid with two more lines drawn to close the shape and one line of symmetry shown as a dashed line.

questions.q_figure: Four unfolded square sheets: (a) two holes at the left and right sides at the same height, (b) two holes close together near the top right corner, (c) two holes on the right edge one above the other, (d) four holes, one near each corner.
questions.s_figure: Each sheet with its fold line drawn as a dashed line: vertical for (a), diagonal for (b), horizontal for (c), and a vertical and a horizontal line for (d).

questions.q_figure: Five shapes, each with one marked hole and a dashed line of symmetry: a square with a diagonal, a square with a horizontal middle line, an equilateral triangle with a vertical line through its top corner, and two circles each with a dashed diameter.
questions.s_figure: Each shape with the second hole drawn as the mirror image of the first across the dashed line.

questions.q_figure: A sheet of paper folded in half vertically with an arrow, labelled Vertical Fold, and a sheet folded in half horizontally with an arrow, labelled Horizontal Fold.

Four cutting pictures: (a) a green sheet folded once with a wavy dotted cut line near its open edge, (b) a green folded sheet with a banner-shaped dotted cut that has an arrow-head notch, (c) a purple sheet folded vertically and then horizontally with notches cut at the corner and the edge, (d) a yellow sheet folded in half with rectangular notches cut along the open edge.
questions.s_figure: Each sheet opened out, showing the hole as the cut shape together with its mirror image across each fold line.

questions.q_figure: Two purple square sheets: one with a square hole in the centre whose sides are parallel to the sheet, and one with a tilted square hole in the centre whose corners point up, down, left and right.
questions.s_figure: A sheet showing the folds as dashed lines and the single straight cut marked at the closed corner for each of the two holes.

questions.name: Example 1: Angles of symmetry of a strip
questions.q_figure: A strip shaped like a trapezium, with its two parallel sides of different lengths and a dot marking its centre.
questions.s_figure: The strip beside its copy turned through 180° about the dot, with the two parallel sides swapped top to bottom.

questions.q_figure: Three figures, each with a dot marked: (a) a plus shape made of two equal rectangles crossing at their middles with the dot at the centre, (b) a vertical line with the dot at its middle and a small square on the right of each end, (c) two long vertical lines joined at their middles by a horizontal bar with the dot at the middle of the bar.
questions.s_figure: Each figure turned about its dot through the angles that bring it back onto itself, shown as small copies.

questions.q_figure: Seven figures: a circle divided into 4 equal parts by a cross, a downward-pointing triangle with a dot inside, a circle divided into 3 equal parts by three spokes, a four-bladed pinwheel, an X made of two crossing lines, a five-pointed star with a dot at its centre, and a shape like the letter B made of a vertical line with two half circles on its right.
questions.s_figure: The same seven figures with the five that have more than one angle of symmetry ringed.

questions.q_figure: Six figures: (a) a slanted line with a dot at its middle and a small flag at each end, (b) an X made of two crossing lines, (c) a six-pointed star with a dot at its centre, (d) three bent arms with fists arranged around a centre, (e) a plus shape made of two rectangles with a dot at the centre, (f) a regular pentagon with a dot at its centre.

questions.name: Radial Arms: 5 and 6 angles of symmetry
questions.s_figure: Two radial-arm figures, one with 5 equal arms and one with 6 equal arms, with the angle between neighbouring arms marked.

questions.name: Order and Angles: multiples of the smallest
Order and Angles: True or False

questions.q_figure: A circle divided into 12 equal sectors, none of them coloured.
questions.s_figure: Circles of 12 sectors coloured to give 3 angles of symmetry and to give 4 angles of symmetry.

questions.q_figure: The Ashoka Chakra, a wheel with 24 equal spokes.

questions.s_figure: Two figures that have both reflection symmetry and rotational symmetry, each with its lines of symmetry dashed and its centre of rotation marked.
Rough sketches of the triangles and quadrilaterals asked for in (a) to (d), each with its lines of symmetry drawn as dashed lines.

questions.q_figure: The new Parliament Building in Delhi beside its outer boundary, a triangle-like outline with its three corners cut off.
questions.s_figure: The outline with its lines of symmetry drawn as dashed lines and its centre marked.

questions.q_figure: The first shape sequence of Chapter 1, Table 3, the regular polygons, drawn in a row: triangle, square, pentagon, hexagon, heptagon, octagon, nonagon and decagon.
questions.s_figure: A table with each regular polygon and its number of lines of symmetry.

questions.q_figure: The first shape sequence of Chapter 1, Table 3, the regular polygons, drawn in a row: triangle, square, pentagon, hexagon, heptagon, octagon, nonagon and decagon.
questions.s_figure: A table with each regular polygon and its number of angles of symmetry.

questions.q_figure: The five shapes of the last shape sequence of Chapter 1, Table 3, the Koch snowflake sequence, drawn in a row.
questions.s_figure: A table with the number of lines of symmetry and the number of angles of symmetry of each of the five shapes.

questions.name: Playing with Tiles a (section 9.2)
questions.q_figure: An 8 by 8 grid of square tiles, each cut by a diagonal into a blue triangle and a yellow triangle, with the top left 4 by 4 quarter already filled and a red vertical line and a red horizontal line through the middle of the grid.
questions.s_figure: The completed 8 by 8 grid with the other three quarters filled as mirror images of the filled quarter and the two red lines marked.

questions.q_figure: One colour tile, a square cut by a diagonal into a blue triangle and a yellow triangle, beside an empty 4 by 4 grid for 16 such tiles.
questions.s_figure: Two filled 4 by 4 tile designs, one with exactly one line of symmetry and one with exactly two lines, each with its lines dashed.

questions.q_figure: One colour tile, a square cut by a diagonal into a blue triangle and a yellow triangle.
questions.s_figure: An example symmetric design made from such tiles with its lines of symmetry dashed.

questions.name: Symmetry Game: strategy on a 6 by 6 grid
questions.q_figure: A 6 by 6 grid with two example lines drawn, one horizontal and one vertical, each covering two adjacent squares, and a small grid showing two overlapping lines marked Not allowed.
questions.s_figure: The 6 by 6 grid with its centre marked, one line of the first player and the reply drawn as its half-turn copy about the centre.
